name: What's the difference between a standard toilet and a raised toilet?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a standard toilet and a raised toilet?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in the height of the toilet bowl. A standard toilet typically measures around 14 to 15 inches from the floor to the top of the bowl (without the seat), whereas a raised toilet, also known as comfort height, is usually 16.5 to 17.5 inches high. This seemingly small difference makes a significant impact on ease of use, especially for taller individuals, seniors, or those with limited mobility, providing a more comfortable and accessible experience.
acceptedAnswer.description: The main difference is height: standard toilets are 14-15 inches, while raised (comfort height) toilets are 16.5-17.5 inches, offering easier use.
